paper.title: Characterization and engineering of a plastic-degrading aromatic polyesterase

thesis: Structure-guided mutation unexpectedly improves PET degradation and broad substrate assays recast PETase as an aromatic polyesterase rather than an enzyme already optimized for PET.

nodes.title: What controls PETase substrate specificity?
nodes.body: Relate PETase structure to polymer degradation and test whether structure-guided engineering can improve activity.

nodes.title: Resolve the enzyme structure
nodes.body: Use long-wavelength X-ray crystallography and comparisons with homologous cutinases.

nodes.title: Atomic-resolution structure
nodes.body: The PETase structure resolves to 0.92 Å and shows an α/β-hydrolase fold with a broader active-site cleft than the closest cutinase homolog.

nodes.title: A broad cleft may explain PET adaptation
nodes.body: The authors initially hypothesized that the unusually broad active site enabled more efficient PET depolymerization.

nodes.title: Make the cleft cutinase-like
nodes.body: Engineer S238F/W159H to narrow the cleft and W185A to test a conserved dynamic residue.

nodes.title: Digest realistic crystalline PET
nodes.body: Compare buffer, wild type and mutants on PET coupons near bottle crystallinity using DSC, SEM, HPLC and NMR.

nodes.title: Double mutant unexpectedly wins
nodes.body: S238F/W159H outperforms wild-type PETase, with 4.13 percentage points more absolute crystallinity loss; W185A performs poorly.

nodes.title: PETase is not fully optimized for PET
nodes.body: The unexpected mutant result contradicts the initial adaptation hypothesis and leaves room for further protein engineering.

nodes.title: Test polymer scope
nodes.body: Incubate wild-type and mutant enzymes with semiaromatic PEF and aliphatic PBS and PLA.

nodes.title: Activity follows aromaticity
nodes.body: PETase degrades PEF, with 15.7% relative crystallinity reduction, but shows no detectable degradation of the tested aliphatic polyesters.

nodes.title: PETase is an aromatic polyesterase
nodes.body: The enzyme's demonstrated scope is better characterized by semiaromatic substrates than by PET alone.

openQuestions: The paper reports failed ligand-bound crystallization attempts, but no run-level lab trace is available to reconstruct.
